what_happened: Discovered task 426 (completed, archived) already diagnosed and fixed the exact cited incident (iss_1792162538950_NYX4YD) on the detection side (RECOVERY_DECLINED phase/dispatch_seq attribution bugs + stall/strand corroboration), and already confirmed planner-agent.md's contract needs no edit. Found the one remaining gap is structural: skill-orchestrate's direct agent dispatch path never calls skill_create_postflight_marker, so the existing SubagentStop enforcement hook (subagent-postflight.sh) cannot fire for this dispatch path at all.

Observed while planning, out of scope here: .postflight-pending has no row in context/standards/orchestrator-runtime-files.md's runtime-file table and no pattern in scripts/lib/runtime-file-patterns.sh, unlike its sibling .postflight-loop-guard which has both. Recorded as a distinct defect class (runtime-file tracking coverage) and explicitly listed as a Non-Goal of this task's plan.

Research established that a completed prior task (426) already closed both fix locations this task names (planner-agent.md's terminal-write contract and orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's STATUS_IN_PROGRESS detection) against the identical cited incident, and that the only remaining gap is structural. The plan collapsed from new enforcement infrastructure to a 2-phase, 3-file documentation change. The structural claim was independently re-verified during planning with one grep rather than taken on trust.

Plan Phase 1's Tier Justification named a literal verify-deploy.sh invocation with TARGET=agent-system/extensions/core, which the script rejects (no deployed .claude tree there); ran the equivalent check with TARGET=repo-root instead, which passed.

Phase 2's edits to skill-lifecycle.md and system-defect-discrimination.md drifted their index-entries.json line_count declarations, failing doc-lint (Rule R). Fixed via the deployed .claude/scripts/generate-context-line-counts.sh --write (source-store copy refuses to run outside a deployed tree). This also incidentally corrected 4 pre-existing, unrelated line_count drifts from sibling tasks already present in the working tree at dispatch start; only the two entries for this task's own files are included in this phase's commit (the containment self-check drops the rest as out-of-scope).
